stories.author: giuliomagnifico
stories.title: AI usage patterns in software teams
stories.groq_label: AI adoption in software teams doubled across all functions in six months, with executives leading the charge.
stories.groq_discussion:
Discussion type: – News Style

Hacker News commenters reacted to the discussion on AI usage patterns in software teams with cautious optimism. Many praised the efficiency gains from AI-assisted coding, noting how it accelerates initial development while shifting focus to code review. However, the discussion also surfaced recurring concerns about measurement accuracy, particularly regarding metrics like pull request volume, which may be inflated by tooling adoption rather than actual increases in development activity. Despite these criticisms, the general sentiment suggests that the community considers AI-driven workflows a promising evolution in software development, though its long-term impact on team dynamics and decision-making remains an open question.
stories.groq_explain: AI adoption in software teams has skyrocketed across all roles—engineers, product managers, designers, even executives—doubling or tripling in just six months. It’s not just coders using it; go-to-market teams are jumping in too. The biggest surprise? Top leaders like CEOs and CTOs are using AI as much as their teams, showing it’s becoming a core tool for decision-making, not just execution. This matters because it signals AI isn’t just a niche productivity hack—it’s reshaping how entire organizations operate, from the top down. The data gives a clear snapshot of where AI-assisted work stands in 2026 and sets a baseline for future trends.
